**Python 3.12 – What’s New (Release Notes)** *Source: https://docs.python.org/3.12/whatsnew/3.12.html* --- ### Major Highlights | Area | New Features / Improvements | |------|------------------------------| | **Interpreter & Runtime** | • **Isolated sub‑interpreters** – each sub‑interpreter now has its own separate GIL and memory, making it safer to run concurrent code.
• **Improved error messages** – more precise syntax‑error locations, clearer suggestions, and better handling of common mistakes. | | **Performance** | • **Zero‑cost exception handling** – the interpreter now avoids the overhead of building traceback objects unless they’re needed.
• **Faster CPython bytecode** – several optimizations (e.g., better handling of `CALL_FUNCTION_EX`, more efficient `LOAD_METHOD`). | | **Standard Library** | • **`zoneinfo`** now supports the IANA time‑zone database directly on Windows.
• **`asyncio`**: new `TaskGroup` API for structured concurrency, plus `asyncio.timeout` context manager.
• **`statistics`**: added `fmean` for floating‑point mean, `multimode`, and `quantiles`.
• **`pathlib`**: `Path.is_relative_to()` and `Path.relative_to()` now accept multiple base paths. | | **Typing** | • **PEP 673 – Self type** – a built‑in `Self` type for annotating methods that return an instance of their class.
• **PEP 646 – Variadic Generics** – support for type‑safe variable‑length tuple types (`*Ts`). | | **Syntax** | • **Pattern Matching Enhancements** – `case` statements can now use `|` for “or” patterns and support `as` bindings inside nested patterns.
• **Parenthesized Context Managers** – `with (a() as x, b() as y):` is now allowed. | | **Debugging & Development** | • **`faulthandler`** now prints the Python traceback for segmentation faults on Windows.
• **`-X dev`** flag enables additional runtime checks (e.g., detecting reference‑count leaks). | | **Build & C‑API** | • **PEP 680 – Stable ABI for the Python C API** – a new stable ABI that allows extension modules to be compiled once and run across multiple CPython versions.
• **New `PyInterpreterState_GetID`** function for identifying interpreter instances. | | **Deprecations & Removals** | • Removal of the `distutils` package (use `setuptools` or `sysconfig`).
• Deprecated `asyncio.get_event_loop()` without an explicit loop argument.
• Several legacy modules (`parser`, `imp`) are now fully removed. | --- ### Quick Links - **Full Release Notes** – https://docs.python.org/3.12/whatsnew/3.12.html - **PEP Index** – https://peps.python.org/ (see PEP 673, PEP 646, PEP 680, etc.) - **Download Python 3.12** – https://www.python.org/downloads/release/python-3120/ --- ### How to Get Started ```bash # Install the latest 3.12 release (example for macOS/Homebrew) brew install python@3.12 # Verify version python3.12 --version # → Python 3.12.x ``` --- **Bottom line:** Python 3.12 focuses on performance, better concurrency primitives, richer typing, and clearer error messages, while also cleaning up older, less‑maintained modules. It’s a solid upgrade for developers who want faster execution and more expressive code.
